title: POC Weekly Velocity Gate Readout - Auriga Labs
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latency and throughput bench results versus the incumbent provider. Redwood presented routing and batching tweaks, found 12-18% p95 latency reduction in hosted config with prefix caching; throughput improved ~22% in the dedicated slot with quantization. Customer raised VPC networking and SOC2 questions; agreement to run a head-to-head 12-hour load blast and share security pack. Next steps: run 12h load, share SSO/KMS notes, schedule on-prem onboarding scoping.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-27
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood CSM), Samir (Auriga Head of ML), Ellen (Auriga Infra), Marco (Auriga CTO), Nora (Data Eng)

[00:00] Jordan: ok hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off — this is the weekly velocity gate readout, quick agenda, bench results vs incumbent, routing/quantize tweaks, and next steps.
[00:18] Samir: yeah thanks, hope you all had a good week. we've been looking at the last runs, interested to see p95 changes.
[00:25] Priya: quick note — ran three config variants: hosted with prefix cache on, hosted without cache, and dedicated slot with int8 quant profile plus batching tweaks. numbers are in the sheet we shared.
[00:40] Ellen: link please? i have the deck open but not the raw traces yet.
[00:44] Jordan: posted again, https://redwood.ai/decks/auriga-bench-2026-03-27 and spreadsheet https://redwood.ai/spreadsheets/auriga-bench-raw-2026-03-27
[00:52] Marco: great, thanks. ok why don't we jump into the headline numbers.

[01:05] Priya: headline — versus IncumbentCloud baseline, hosted with prefix caching reduced p95 latency by about 12% on the conversational load (avg prompt 120 tokens, response 140 tokens). p99 improved ~9%. For the dedicated slot with int8 quant and continuous batching, we saw throughput increase ~22% (tokens/sec) and p95 down about 18% compared to baseline dedicated runs.
[01:30] Samir: that's promising, can you give absolute numbers? p95 and p99?
[01:36] Priya: sure — baseline p95 was ~420ms; hosted w/cache is ~370ms p95. Baseline p99 ~980ms, hosted w/cache around ~890ms. Dedicated slot baseline p95 ~380ms, with quant/batch ~310ms. throughput baseline tokens/sec was ~9.1k, we saw ~11.1k in dedicated config.
[02:01] Nora: those tokens/sec are for batch size 8 or 16?
[02:05] Priya: batch size varied — for latency-focused runs we kept batch 8, for throughput runs we used batch 16 with dynamic batching and a 20ms batching window.

[02:20] Ellen: any change in hallucination or quality? we can't sacrifice accuracy for speed.
[02:25] Priya: we ran the prompt set QA check, Rouge and some custom evals — delta was within noise, top-level rounding errors only on very long outputs. Quantization introduced a couple low-confidence tokens but no systemic degradation. We flagged 3 prompts out of 1,200 where completion token probability dips — details in sheet.

[02:50] Samir: good. about the routing and fallback playbook — what happens when the dedicated pool is saturated? we saw in earlier runs your fallback sent to a smaller model which changed outputs.
[03:03] Jordan: yes, that's expected. our playbook default is route by latency tier, then fallback to compatible variant with preserved semantic parity. we can configure auto-fallback to route to the hosted pool rather than a smaller model if you prefer consistency.
[03:20] Marco: important for us to keep deterministic outputs for auditability, so prefer hosted fallback over smaller model. can we map that in the config?
[03:29] Priya: yep — it's a routing policy param, we call it preferred_fallback_targets, we can pin it to hosted-similar-model. note: that may change cost profile.

[03:45] Luis: just a flag — cost delta will be in the sheet; routing to hosted fallback increased unit cost approx 8-12% under heavy fallback conditions.

[03:55] Ellen: network — our infra team worried about egress and cold start from the VPC side. what was the network overhead you measured?
[04:02] Priya: in our VPC-simulated runs we saw an additional median network overhead of ~25-40ms depending on cross-AZ hops. you also saw spikes when NAT throughput throttled in some sim configs.
[04:14] Ellen: hmm, we run strict egress policies and limited NAT gateways. that could add 50-80ms in worst-case which would blow SLA.
[04:21] Jordan: noted — we need your topology to simulate exact numbers. Ellen, can you share the VPC diagram?
[04:25] Ellen: i'll drop it in the thread after the call.

[04:32] Samir: vendor lock-in risk — we still need clarity on data retention and key management. Is KMS integrated for private deployments?
[04:40] Priya: yes. Private deployments support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, and HSM via partners). In hosted mode we do envelope encryption with customer KMS integration options. we'll share the security pack.
[04:53] Marco: and SOC2 / compliance? we need the doc set.
[04:56] Luis: i'm on that — we'll send SOC2 report excerpt, RBAC model, audit log samples. Deliver by Tuesday.

[05:05] Nora: on the dedicated bench, you mentioned continuous batching and KV caching — can you explain the cache invalidation pattern? we do session affinity and KV reuse for chat — if cache misses spike, performance drops.
[05:16] Priya: good question. KV (K-V) cache persists per conversation for up to 30 minutes by default; invalidation on explicit session end or after TTL. For voicey/long-stream loads we bump TTL to 2 hours. misses were below 6% in our tests. we can tune TTL for your workload.

[05:35] Samir: what about warm-start cost? if we pin dedicated slots, what's the warm-up latency when model first loads?
[05:41] Priya: model load time ~45-70 seconds depending on quant profile and GPU; we have pre-warm policies and can keep a hot spare to reduce cold start to under 5s for most traffic patterns. there's a small cost for hot spares (~5% extra).

[05:55] Ellen: can you run a continuous 12-hour blast to compare endpoint breakdowns vs IncumbentCloud at our typical traffic mix? we need to see long-run variance and tail behavior.
[06:03] Jordan: yes — we'll schedule that, Priya will run in the dedicated slot and mirror the incumbent traffic.
[06:09] Priya: i'll do one run with continuity (no restarts) and another with rolling restarts to simulate infra flaps. we'll capture p95/p99, error rates, and unit cost per 1M tokens.

[06:20] Marco: what's the unit-cost delta we're expecting on dedicated vs incumbent? rough numbers.
[06:24] Jordan: based on current commits, raw inference unit cost is around 14% lower on Redwood dedicated with the quant profile; hosted cost parity varies by request shape, but hosted with caching is around +2% cost and better latency. we'll provide a line-item cost ladder in the sheet.

[06:40] Samir: legal/procurement will want data residency proofs and audit trail details. who owns the audit logs in Private?
[06:47] Priya: in Private deployments logs are under customer control; audit events forwarded to your S3 or equivalent; we support TTL and server-side encryption with your KMS.

[06:55] Nora: any gotchas for our streaming endpoint (tooling with websockets)?
[06:58] Priya: streaming is supported; note that KV cache rehydration for streaming has slightly higher memory pressure but latency profile is similar. tuning concurrency at the proxy layer helps.

[07:10] Jordan: quick callout — we noticed in your earlier artifact that some prompts had very long system messages that trip attention window; trimming those reduced median latency by 40ms. small prompt engineering wins.
[07:22] Samir: ha, yeah our research team had long system preambles. good to know.

[07:28] Marco: okay, circling back to rollout: if the 12-hour blast looks good, what's the path to production?
[07:35] Jordan: plan A: start with a canary routing 5% traffic to Redwood hosted, monitor quality and latency for 48 hours, then increase to 25% with dedicated reserved capacity, then do full cutover. We'll include fallback to incumbent for safety.
[07:47] Ellen: timeline — we aim to decide by april 6th for pilot production gating.
[07:51] Luis: noted in next steps, we'll aim to have bench results by march 31st to hit that decision date.

[08:05] Priya: any blockers from Auriga side?
[08:08] Samir: need VPC topology, legal to get SOC2 excerpts, and infra lead to agree to NAT adjustments for the 12-hour run.
[08:14] Ellen: i'll coordinate NAT staging.

[08:20] Jordan: perfect. quick recap and owners — (1) Redwood runs 12-hr head-to-head (Priya) (2) Redwood shares detailed bench spreadsheet and raw traces (Jordan) (3) Redwood security pack + SOC2 excerpts (Luis) (4) Auriga shares VPC diagram and egress constraints (Ellen) (5) schedule next technical deep-dive after 12hr run (Jordan/Luis).

[08:44] Samir: thanks everyone, appreciate the granular numbers. one ask — can you surface p50, p95, p99 and unit cost per million tokens in the next sheet? makes procurement easier.
[08:55] Priya: absolutely, will add columns for p50/p95/p99/op-cost-per-1M.

[09:05] Marco: final Q — any known limitation on multi-tenant telemetry? we need per-customer tracing.
[09:11] Priya: we emit request-scoped traces and can mask PII; we can set retention to 90 days for immediate needs, longer with enterprise add-on.

[09:20] Jordan: ok if no other questions we'll wrap. thanks all.

End notes: shared artifacts: deck and spreadsheet links above, raw traces delivered to shared drive.
